name: Eragrostis

project_scope.selection_mode: structural learner batch / B135 source-status reconciliation
project_scope.note: All seven source concepts are installed canonical learner species. E. hirsuta remains native-range HOLD/UNRESOLVED and excluded from confirmed-native metrics; admission does not imply native PASS.

recognition.where_to_look_first: Do not start with flower color. Start with panicle architecture and then inspect the sheath/collar: openness, branch angle, spikelet clustering, glands, and where the hairs sit are the fast field characters in the project set.
priority: open airy panicle versus contracted/coarse panicle
widely spaced spikelets versus dense clusters along branches
glands on panicle parts or lemmas
leaf width and whether blades are flat or involute

quick_split: E. cilianensis — annual, coarse many-flowered spikelets, often crater-like glands; odor can support the ID.
E. intermedia — tufted perennial with a very open transparent panicle, long divergent pedicels, and mostly smooth sheaths.
E. lugens — narrow firm involute leaves and a comparatively restrained panicle.
E. secundiflora — conspicuous dense clusters of spikelets along ascending panicle branches, often violet to reddish.
E. spectabilis — broad airy purple cloud with widely spreading flexible branches; mature inflorescence can tumble.
E. trichodes — tall perennial with long hairs concentrated at the sheath throat/collar and a huge diffuse fine-branched panicle.
comparison_lesson.hold_comparison: E. hirsuta — CANONICAL LEARNER, native-range HOLD/UNRESOLVED (not a confirmed target native). Look for hairs on sheaths and panicle branch axils; compare against E. intermedia and E. trichodes. Preserve uncertainty.

look_here_first: 1 — Find the grass sheath, collar and ligule, then note whether hairs cover the sheath SURFACE or mainly appear at the THROAT.
2 — Confirm a true open branched panicle and locate a complete mature spikelet on one pedicel.
3 — Photograph several branch axils; hirsuta often shows bearded axils, but occasional hairs alone do not diagnose it.
4 — Compare relative tuft size, leaf arching and flowering cloud as supportive characters only.
5 — If either sheath character or spikelet structure is missing, leave Eragrostis sp.; do not force species from purple tone.
overlap_cautions: E. intermedia and E. trichodes can both form open panicles; sheath/collar hair location helps.
E. hirsuta is already installed but remains native-range unresolved; no native PASS implied.
Panicle shape changes with maturity and wind; compare mature, intact specimens.
study_strategy.current_training_priority: MANUAL FIELD CARD ENRICHMENT · Eragrostis intermedia vs hirsuta vs trichodes
study_strategy.triad_warning: Descriptions and hair placement can vary, especially near collar and branch axils. A shaggy sheath favors E. hirsuta, throat-concentrated hairs and a huge fine panicle favor E. trichodes, and mostly smooth sheaths with an open ovate panicle favor E. intermedia. The three current galleries do not contain a matched, same-scale collar macro trio.

trio_field_key.question: Are conspicuous long hairs visible along much of the sheath BODY?
trio_field_key.if_yes: E. hirsuta is favored; confirm bearded lower panicle axils and reproductive parts.
trio_field_key.if_no: Compare E. intermedia and E. trichodes; photograph the sheath throat and mature head.
trio_field_key.warning: A missing or poorly focused sheath cannot be scored as smooth.

trio_field_key.question: Is the plant tall with a very large, diffuse, often oblong head and obvious hairs concentrated at sheath throat?
trio_field_key.if_yes: E. trichodes is a candidate; look for small spikelets on fine branches, sometimes tending toward their tips.
trio_field_key.if_no: E. intermedia may be favored by smaller open ovate head and near-smooth sheaths away from collar.
trio_field_key.warning: Panicle size, branch-tip clustering and collar hairs overlap, not proof by themselves.

trio_field_key.question: Are the ligule and mature spikelets visible with appropriate magnification?
trio_field_key.if_yes: Check a published flora key and actual measurements before species finality.
trio_field_key.if_no: Use Eragrostis sp. as the scientifically responsible field label.

study_strategy.scientific_safety: Statewide nativity of E. hirsuta does not certify Hays/project-native status; preserve its existing range-unresolved classification. Comparisons discuss appearance only, not nativity.

look_here_first: GRASS FIRST: confirm a real node/sheath, a short hair-fringe ligule and small several-flowered spikelets; then LOVEGRASS: use the whole panicle branch pattern, sheath hair distribution and mature spikelet anatomy. FOR THIS THREE-WAY SET, inspect hair ACROSS the sheath (hirsuta) versus mainly at the mouth (intermedia/trichodes), then compare a complete mature panicle. Color or a transparent seedhead alone never settles species.
shared_traits: Poaceae with spikelets bearing multiple florets and usually many small, overlapping lemmas.
Panicle branching and spikelet spacing vary across the seven installed lovegrasses.
Leaf sheath, collar/ligule, branch axils and lemma details are often more diagnostic than flower color.

species_comparison_matrix.measurement_protocol: Measure panicle length/width and spikelet length in mm on mature attached material; record branch angles and hair positions. Numeric species cutoffs are intentionally not invented where current sources lack verified measurements.

quick_key.if: The sheath surface/margins have conspicuous long spreading hairs, not just a tuft at the blade junction
quick_key.then: Favor Eragrostis hirsuta; next inspect hairy panicle branch axils and mature spikelets.

quick_key.if: Sheath body is comparatively smooth, but the throat/collar has hairs; flowering head open and ovate
quick_key.then: Favor Eragrostis intermedia; compare with sand, purple and other airy lovegrasses.

quick_key.if: Tall bunch with long arching leaves, a particularly large diffuse panicle and long hairs at sheath THROAT
quick_key.then: Favor Eragrostis trichodes; verify glabrous stem nodes and spikelets.

quick_key.if: Panicle silhouette is known, but collar/sheath hairs or spikelets cannot be observed
quick_key.then: Eragrostis sp. — get photos of sheath surface, ligule, lower branch axils and a mature spikelet.

quick_key.if: Head is red-purple with dense clustered spikelets along ascending branches
quick_key.then: Review E. secundiflora before calling one of the airy trio.

quick_key.if: Very broad loose purple panicle that may detach/tumble
quick_key.then: Review E. spectabilis; color alone is not decisive.

quick_key.if: Coarser many-flowered spikelets and glandular portions on an annual
quick_key.then: Review introduced E. cilianensis; inspect glands, not odor alone.

quick_key.if: Narrow inward-rolled leaves, more restrained seedhead
quick_key.then: Review E. lugens; confirm with spikelet and sheath characters.

visual_comparison.title: Lovegrasses — compare actual sheaths and reproductive parts
visual_comparison.subtitle: Three real canonical exact-source photographs arranged to teach the most important structural distinction. Not a matched-scale comparison; all taxon IDs follow source determinations.
visual_comparison.memory_rule: HAIR ALL ALONG SHEATH = hirsuta candidate; hairy throat + very large fine head = trichodes candidate; largely smooth sheath + open oval head = intermedia candidate. Verify with magnification.
